distinguishing_features: Uses impressed current to cathodically polarize the titanium surface rather than dosing a chemical inhibitor.
Proposes reference-electrode feedback to control the surface potential.
Applies the approach to a working chlor-alkali anode and its coating substrate.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce corrosion-related degradation of titanium anode components in chlor-alkali anolyte while maintaining cell operation.
parsed.viable_reason: Cathodically polarizing a working anode would suppress its anodic chlorine-evolution function, and the proposed potential and coupon test do not establish protection under operating anode conditions.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Cathodic protection is a familiar corrosion-control approach, so applying it to corrosion is an obvious general step even though it is incompatible with the anode’s required operation.
